stimuli.description: Nine real hills on the University of Virginia grounds with inclinations from 2° to 34° (2°, 4°, 5°, 6°, 10°, 21°, 31°, 33°, 34°).

Twelve computer-simulated virtual reality hills with inclinations ranging from 5° to 60° at 5° increments. Each hill was grassy with a black and white checkerboard road, placed on a large ground plane with a sky blue background.
Two real hills (5° and 31°) on the University of Virginia grounds.

limitations: It is not known whether the influence of viewpoint on the haptic measure was due to differential ease in adjusting the palm board across the two viewpoints, or to the effect of some variable that caused a genuine change in haptic perception.

The authors acknowledge that the alternative explanation for the dissociation between conscious perception and motoric action (recalibration of motor programs) is not definitively ruled out, stating 'We think that this alternative is less plausible than the separate visual systems account, but we have no evidence against it.'
